He's just the best boss I've worked for.”
DM: Be a very big goblin or—so, like, points up at Acescale. “His size.”
DM: He like points at all of you. “Catch people, obviously. He only wants one every week. We're set for the next month with you 4.”
Dilion: Does it have to be people? And ask, or I get to Loria, to translate unless someone else is also speaking.
DM: We sent a dwarf up there once. Certainly happy with halflings. Makes us dress em nice before we send them off.
Unknown: Just the halflings, or everybody?
DM: Oh, everybody, some of them in armor, some in nice clothes. There was a merchant a few weeks back he wanted bound in a white robe, for some reason.
Dilion: Hey? They don't come back out. Yes.
DM: Nobody's ever come out. All the gold and treasure and all the people. But he lets us keep silver copper, good—
Loria: Where? Where do you take the prisoners dress nicely to seek where?
DM: The manor obviously. This is stupid.
Loria: Yes, yes, not bit panicked.
Loria: Can you point to where?
DM: Check your eyes. Look out there. The Manor, the big villa!
DM: Never seen him leave. Why would he? Been here for months.
Acescale: Well, I guess we've really got all that we need from this guy.
DM: Fools, haven’t got all you need. I'm gonna show you. Just you wait.
DM: My army to come up. 10 goblins loyal to me.
Dilion: But it's only 5. There's like 5, 3 had. Drop it. If you're—
Acescale: If you're dead, who are they loyal to?
DM: If I'm dead, they'll attack with such a vicious vengeance to get revenge for my death that you won't know what hit you.
Dilion: Attack us, anyway, so your life is kind of forfeit now.
Acescale: Still, a lot of gambling.
DM: Well, you'll never get past the gate guards, anyway.

Dilion: Are they really tricky work? Huh! These gate guards! What are they? What are they like? Am I right? Like, “Oh, be ashamed to know what details they you could give about them.” They got more than one man. That's what I'm guessing.
DM: Spits on the ground. “Those filthy krekka. Grimstone trusts them more than anyone.” Loria, you recognize this as a goblin slur for hobgoblins.
Loria: Where is where is Ulgna right now?
DM: She's probably running away. That pathetic coward. Nobody's loyal to her.
Loria: Don't you work for Ulgna?
DM: “Fool! Who told you that?” He like strains against his ropes to try and bite you.
DM: Morky is a drunk idiot.

DM: Grimstone trusts me. Ulgna never liked him. Spits on the ground. I'm the one who has the loyalty. I'm the one he picks. Damn Ulgna! She'd probably run away in the tunnels if she was left to her own devices.
DM: I don't pay anybody—for Grimstone pays me. I pay my loyal lackeys. That's why they'll fight to the death to save me, I promise you.

Acescale: Okay. Well, the way that you're talking to us, I think there's like a 95% chance you might not make it through another sentence. So have you got an entrance into these tunnels we can use to get in past the hob goblins, or are you like done breathing now?
DM: He he kind of laughed at you. “You don't scare me. It's—”
Gaudin: No, not nothing tech. We're gonna just, are we just gonna end this guy here? We could.
Dilion: We've got. I think he's just gonna insult us more. And I don’t think he's gonna give us anything more useful than we've already got.
Gaudin: It is still pissed off about being kicked. So, oh, I'm gonna Eldritch Blast him at point blank range.

DM: Not expecting the—are you still? Do you still? Are you still disguised right? Just like totally had tuned you out, thinking you were just like a goblin in the background, totally, not expecting, like laughing at this lizard folk who didn't really scare him, and then blam, just keels over.
Acescale: I—I cure wounds on him. And and I say, I say, in in common, I say, “We can do this all day.”
Gaudin: I let the the crackling of the blast be right by his ear, just letting him know.
DM: ((Intimidation mechanics)) He just—he like his face drains of color. And he like looks up at you like scared like demeanor shifts entirely like, “No! What do you? What do you want?”
Acescale: That's a tunnel sounded kind of cool. A map of the manor that you know. Like, what have you got?

DM: I've never been in the manor. The tunnels, they lead in what—the—the wine cellar, but does 2—2 entrances that I know. There's—there's one in—in the barracks. I don't think the goblins will let you in. There's one from—from the kitchen, think, in the old gardens near the manor, the walled garden. There's a—there's a—there's a—there's a kitchen there.

And someone said—someone said—someone said there's—there's a chapel on the other side of the manor, and that the—the tunnel might go there. But—but—but I—I haven't been. That's where I look. But that—the hobgoblins just keep us from—from—from—from running. They don't patrol the grounds. Just—just—just stay away from the gates.
Unknown: So the hobgoblins watch the the gates like the the exit from this whole complex, not the gates to the manor?

DM: “There are additional guards that guard the main door to the manor,” he says, but it sounds from him, from the way he says that, there's like only light patrols. Like, one of the hobgoblins will come do a check, like, you know, once a night or something, but it's really—they trust that they're keeping—the goblins are the ones who are supposed to down—stay on guard, and the hobgoblins never go into the tunnels. They're too narrow and uncomfortable.
The implication being, if you wanted to lie low, then you trust this guy not to try and betray you, that tunnels would be pretty safe.
Loria: How many goblins are in the barracks still?
DM: I wasn't lying. There's 10 plus Ulgna.
Acescale: It was kitchen, chapel, or tunnels to the wine cellar? Or are there tunnels to the kitchen in the chapel as well?
DM: The tunnels, the tunnels lead to the wine cellar. The entrances that he knows of. There's a whole tunnel system.
DM: An entrance from the Goblin's barracks. There's an entrance from the kitchen, and there is a rumored entrance from the chapel, but he's never been there.
Acescale: The kitchen you have to be inside to get the tunnels?

DM: No, the kitchens—the kitchen is like, so there's that walled garden that you couldn't see into. That's where the kitchen is. It's it's, you know, a few 100 feet from the manor itself. Presumably from the wine cellar you can get into the manor.
DM: But the goblins never go into the manor.

DM: They can tell you that there's the hobgoblins guard the gates to leave this complex and hobgoblins guard the front door to the manor. And then there's one—there's, yeah, one hobgoblin that does a round every night, just to check and make sure the goblins aren't stirring up trouble. But there are not heavy patrols.

lines: Loria: But we have to figure out what to do with—sorry Tim. What's his name again?
